title: You’re not tired because the race is long.
paragraphs: You’re not tired because the race is long.
You’re tired because you’ve been running while carrying what God told you to drop.
And deep down… you know it.

You smile in public.
You serve in ministry.
You lift your hands in worship.

Because shame is heavy.
Because secret sin drains strength.
Because pretending to be okay is exhausting.
And here’s the tension nobody talks about:

You can look like you’re running…
and still be spiritually stuck.

You can be moving…
and still be dying inside.

That man in the dust—
that’s not just a scene.
But secretly wondering if we even have the strength to stand again.
And this is where the Word of God cuts deep—

“Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith…” (Hebrews 12:1–2, ESV)

Not manage.
Not hide.
Not justify.
Because some of you aren’t just carrying struggles…
You’re carrying things Jesus already died for.

It wraps around your thoughts.
It whispers in your quiet moments.
It tells you, “You’ve gone too far.”
But here’s the truth that breaks chains—
“For the joy that was set before Him, He endured the cross, despising the shame…” (Hebrews 12:2)
He saw the nights you regret.
And He still chose the cross.
Jesus already despised it on your behalf.
Jesus already paid for it in full.
You don’t receive grace by holding on to sin.
You receive grace by surrendering it.
“Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.” (Hebrews 4:16)
You don’t clean yourself first and then come to Jesus.

You are more sinful than you want to admit—
but more loved than you ever imagined.
Jesus Christ, the Son of God, lived the life you couldn’t live.
Then He died the death you deserved.
“So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” (John 8:36)
That secret compromise no one knows?
That shame from your past you refuse to release?
That pride telling you, “You can fix this on your own”?
Because you were never meant to run this race weighed down by chains Christ already broke.
God is not standing at the finish line disappointed in you.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” (Romans 8:1)
That means your past doesn’t get the final word.
If this hit something deep in you…
